title: Black pill bottom navigation with expanding active label

color.method: Pixel sampling via median-cut quantization of the supplied JPEG/GIF (compressed images, so values are approximate within a few units). Entries marked 'approx' were judged by eye, not sampled.
color.roles: Fully achromatic: white card, black capsules, dark-grey active chip, white icons and label.

observed.layout: Five stacked frames of the same 5-item bar (Home, Category, Cart, Save, Profile), each showing a different active tab. Each bar is a full-radius capsule.
observed.hierarchy: Active item is the only one with a label, a filled icon and a chip behind it; inactive items are outline icons only.
observed.typography: Small geometric sans label in white, sentence case (Poppins-like; unconfirmed).
observed.iconography: Outline for inactive, filled for active, which gives two redundant state cues beyond the label.
observed.materials: Flat. No gradients or shadows inside the bars; the card has a soft shadow.

implementation_notes: Active chip width animates to fit icon + label while others stay icon-width; flex with width/max-width transition or a shared layout animation.
State = filled icon variant + label reveal + chip fill.
Frames are a static storyboard of one component, so the transition itself is not visible.
interpretation.caveat: Motion is inferred; the image is static.

concept_work.essence: Only the current destination gets words; everything else gets out of the way.
what_makes_it_work: Three simultaneous active cues (fill, label, chip) mean state is never color-dependent.
Equal icon spacing keeps the bar stable.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Icon-only inactive tabs fail discoverability for ambiguous icons (Save, Category).
The width change shifts neighbors; must be animated smoothly and respect reduced-motion.
Needs accessible names on every icon and a 44-48px touch target.

lessons: Showing the label only on the active tab saves width but costs discoverability; choose icons that are universally understood.
Redundant state cues are good accessibility.
